Why all three layers miss it: (a) _independence_harness patches the MODULE ATTRIBUTE episode_capture.reopen_total, but _rt_alias holds the original function object bound at import, so nothing raises; (b) the AST scan collects identifiers from _ControlRun.expectations and checks them against FORBIDDEN_IDENTIFIERS - it sees '_rt_alias', which is not in the set, and 'reopen_total' never appears as a Name or an Attribute anywhere in the scanned source; (c) the prose is untouched. The docstring of test_every_field_has_a_named_independent_source says layer (b) exists because '(a) is defeated by exactly one thing: a name bound at import time (from episode_capture import reopen_total), which no attribute patch can reach' - that is precisely the binding used here, and adding ' as _rt_alias' defeats layer (b) too. HARM IS BOUNDED, measured not reasoned (N1b): I re-ran N1 together with a REAL under-count defect in episode_capture.reopen_total (run-scoped 2 collapsed to step-scoped 1; liveness __NC_MUT__='N1b' from a spawned subprocess and in-process, blob 8a38e33d1c12 -> 0d685836c450). n2-plan-authored-strings.finding: GREEN - NOVEL FINDING (F2, followup-grade). This is the THIRD census blind spot the handoff asked for, found the way the commander found the second: measured, not reasoned. Mutation N2: the parent run's work_id (and its directory, which must move with it per #360) replaced with the hand-typed sentence 'ctl-parent-a-run-id-I-typed-by-hand-as-narrative-prose'. Liveness: blob 796dd5297982 -> 66954add7598, all three replacements hit-count asserted. RESULT: 15 passed, exit 0. FULLY GREEN, including test_control_records_nothing_agent_authored. EFFECT PROVEN AT THE SEAM, not inferred: I read the snapshot episode_capture wrote on its own from the pytest tmp dir - {'run': 'ctl-parent-a-run-id-I-typed-by-hand-as-narrative-prose', 'project': 'mechanical-control-repo', 'role': 'commander', 'spine-step': 'g2'}. A hand-authored sentence is sitting in the  MECHANICAL field. ROOT CAUSE: the census is a scan of _flag_pairs over run.calls, i.e. FLAGS ON ISSUED ARGV ONLY. It structurally cannot see (i) the plan file's contents, where work_id -> the  field and each gate id -> the  field, both hand-authored strings that DO feed the group under test; (ii) the '--file <path>' prefix, which _ControlRun._run prepends to the real argv but deliberately does NOT record in self.calls, so the path the harness composes is invisible to the census by construction; (iii) the temp repo directory name, which feeds . So the docstring's headline claim - 'the control hands the engine exactly TWO agent-supplied strings' - is false as a count: there are at least five, and THREE of them (run, spine-step, project) feed mechanical fields, versus the one (role) that is disclosed. This is exactly the V4 shape the commander itself found and fixed on --claimed-by, still present on three further fields. IMPORTANT CALIBRATION: this is NOT a demand for a prose-detector. The commander's own reasoning - 'role must be SOME supplied string, so a guard demanding no string reach it would be unfalsifiable theatre' - applies verbatim to run, spine-step and project, and I agree with it. The defect is the sentence, not the missing guard: the census asserts a two-element set and the docstring reads that as proof of a global count it does not measure. The honest claim is scoped - 'exactly two agent-supplied strings appear as FLAG VALUES on the issued argv' - and the fix is one sentence, not new machinery.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Doctrine for this run: assert against the behaviour, never against text that describes it. Check every docstring claim in the diff against what the code actually enforces.
r4-quality.finding: FAIL on the runs own governing doctrine - assert against the behaviour, never against text that describes it - which this file still violates in two places, both found by measurement. (1) FIX 2s docstring says layer (b) exists because (a) is defeated by exactly one thing: a name bound at import time, which no attribute patch can reach. Measured N1: adding as _rt_alias to that exact import defeats layer (b) as well, and the suite stays at 15 passed. The text describes a guarantee the code does not provide. (2) The census docstring says the control hands the engine exactly TWO agent-supplied strings. Measured N2: a hand-typed sentence in work_id lands in the run mechanical field with the census green. ANSWERING THE COMMANDERS DIRECT ASK - I enumerated all 31 flags the engine accepts from its argparse block and diffed them against AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS. 14 are unnamed. Ten are genuinely not agent-composed free text (--dry-run/--force/--mechanical are store_true; --which and --result have choices; --file/--worktree/--from-child/--delta are paths; --session-id is a structural id). FOUR carry agent-composed strings and are still unnamed: --evidence (the commanders own V2, still absent), --type (attach, required=True with NO choices, i.e. an arbitrary string), --from (flag-candidate), and --cond (attest). THE THIRD BLIND SPOT IS --cond, and it is sharper than F2 because it is INSIDE the censuss own stated scope: --cond is SANCTIONED in ALLOWED_FLAGS[attest], its value c1 is a string the harness itself authored in _plan, it is passed as a flag value on an issued argv, and because AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS does not name it, it never enters text_bearing. So even restricted to argv flag values the exactly two claim is false - the true statement is exactly two among the subset of flags I chose to call text-bearing. --evidence/--type/--from are covered by the closed-world arm (attach and flag-candidate are not sanctioned verbs), which is the right defence and is the commanders own V2 conclusion; --cond is not covered by anything, only harmless because it feeds no mechanical field. ON THE COMMANDERS EXPLICIT QUESTION - you asked me to say plainly if your reasoning about NOT adding a looks-like-prose guard on role is wrong. It is NOT wrong; I agree with it fully. role must be some supplied string, and a prose-detector would be exactly the unfalsifiable theatre you named. But that reasoning justifies the DECISION, not the SENTENCE - and it applies verbatim to run, spine-step and project, three more fields in identical positions that the sentence does not acknowledge. The fix is to scope the claim in one sentence, not to build machinery. VERIFIED HOLDING, by contrast: the _flag_pairs docstring claims a value beginning with -- makes the census strictly MORE likely to fire, never less. Measured N5 (REOPEN_REASON set to --why=agent prose smuggled past the pair parser): 1 failed, 14 passed, violations = [parent: reopen carries un-sanctioned flag --why=agent prose smuggled past the pair parser=None, ...] x4. Claim holds behaviourally. That is the standard the other two docstrings should meet.

r4-quality: FAIL on the runs own governing doctrine - assert against the behaviour, never against text that describes it - which this file still violates in two places, both found by measurement. (2) The census docstring says the control hands the engine exactly TWO agent-supplied strings. Measured N2: a hand-typed sentence in work_id lands in the run mechanical field with the census green. ANSWERING THE COMMANDERS DIRECT ASK - I enumerated all 31 flags the engine accepts from its argparse block and diffed them against AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS. 14 are unnamed. Ten are genuinely not agent-composed free text (--dry-run/--force/--mechanical are store_true; --which and --result have choices; --file/--worktree/--from-child/--delta are paths; --session-id is a structural id). FOUR carry agent-composed strings and are still unnamed: --evidence (the commanders own V2, still absent), --type (attach, required=True with NO choices, i.e. an arbitrary string), --from (flag-candidate), and --cond (attest). THE THIRD BLIND SPOT IS --cond, and it is sharper than F2 because it is INSIDE the censuss own stated scope: --cond is SANCTIONED in ALLOWED_FLAGS[attest], its value c1 is a string the harness itself authored in _plan, it is passed as a flag value on an issued argv, and because AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS does not name it, it never enters text_bearing. triage_candidates.statement: F1: the FIX 2 independence guard is evaded by an ALIASED import (from episode_capture import reopen_total as _rt_alias) - layer (a) patches the module attribute the alias bypassed, layer (b) scans for the bare identifier and sees only the alias. Measured: 15 passed, fully green, with the oracle deriving its ground truth from the producer under test. Harm is bounded (the literal [1,2,3,4] tuple and R4 catch the version that carries a real defect), so this is a hardening followup, not a blocker. Cheapest fix: have layer (b) reject any name in the scanned scope whose bound object is identical to a FORBIDDEN_PRODUCERS function - an identity check over the module globals, which no aliasing can dodge - or simply correct the docstring to say what layer (b) actually covers.

F2: the census docstring claim 'the control hands the engine exactly TWO agent-supplied strings' is false as a global count and false even within the census's own scope. Measured: a hand-typed sentence in work_id lands in the 'run' MECHANICAL field with the suite at 15 passed (seam snapshot read directly to prove it). The census sees only flag values on recorded argv, so it cannot see the plan file (work_id -> run, gate id -> spine-step), the --file path (deliberately not recorded), or the repo dir name (-> project). Separately, --cond is SANCTIONED for attest, carries a harness-authored string, and is absent from AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS, so it never enters text_bearing - the third blind spot, inside the census's own scope. No new machinery is warranted (the commander's unfalsifiable-theatre reasoning is correct); the fix is to scope the sentence to what is measured and add --cond, --evidence, --type, --from to AGENT_TEXT_FLAGS.

F3: the control fixture stages exactly ONE artifact path, so the artifact-ref field's multi-element behaviour is untested and the out[:1] truncation (attempt 1's M8/F4) remains undetectable as shipped. MEASURED FIX: staging a second file in the fixture makes that same truncation go RED in three tests with 'assert [artifact-ref] == []'. One extra staged file; the comparison machinery already handles it correctly. Cheapest hardening available in the file.
